item.title: Can $100 become $4,000 in a month of trading? I simulated it 2,500 times
item.description: Lolo's Ledger has a goal reality check: a Monte Carlo simulation that tells a trader, before they start, whether their target is possible at safe risk.

item.title: A credit-score cutoff is a business decision, not a model output
item.description: LoanLens scores 55,518 real Prosper loans. The model ranks borrowers; the cutoff that decides who gets a loan comes from a policy table.

item.title: If you can't retrain it twice and get the same numbers, you can't trust them
item.description: Moniguard's metrics used to change on every run. Three small fixes made the retrain reproducible, and CI now proves it on every retrain.

item.title: Letting managers ask data questions in plain English, safely
item.description: How my BI agent keeps metrics consistent with a semantic layer, and why its SQL guard parses queries instead of matching text.

item.title: Why my fraud model reports PR-AUC, not accuracy
item.description: In Moniguard, about 2.8% of transactions are fraud. Here is why accuracy would flatter a useless model, and what I report instead.
